treasure_bohemian_garnets.name: Bohemian Garnet Cluster
treasure_bohemian_garnets.lore: Blood-red garnets still growing in their lump of rock, the kind Bohemian jewellers set by the hundred into brooches, combs and buttons. One is not worth much. A handful buys a horse.

treasure_baltic_amber.name: Lump of Baltic Amber
treasure_baltic_amber.lore: Tree resin that set hard forty million years ago and washed up on the cold Baltic shore. Roman traders walked a thousand miles north along the Amber Road to buy it. This lump holds a gnat that was trapped before there were people to trap anything.

treasure_badakhshan_lapis.name: Badakhshan Lapis Stone
treasure_badakhshan_lapis.lore: Blue stone from the mountain mines of Badakhshan, dug for six thousand years. Ground to powder it became ultramarine, the blue painters saved for their most important robes because it cost more than gold. The golden flecks are pyrite: fool's gold, for once doing an honest job.

treasure_burmese_ruby.name: Burmese Ruby
treasure_burmese_ruby.lore: A ruby from the Mogok valley in Burma, the red the gem trade calls pigeon's blood. Burma's kings claimed every large stone the miners dug up. This one got away.

treasure_kashmir_sapphire.name: Kashmir Sapphire
treasure_kashmir_sapphire.lore: In the 1880s a landslide high in the mountains of Kashmir uncovered sapphires the soft blue of cornflowers. The mine was worked out within a few years, and nothing like those stones has been found since.

treasure_golconda_diamond.name: Golconda Diamond
treasure_golconda_diamond.lore: From the mines near Golconda in India, which gave the world the Koh-i-Noor and the Hope. For two thousand years India was the only place on earth where diamonds were found. It is cut the old Indian way, to keep as much of the stone as the cutter dared.

treasure_idol_eye.name: Eye of a Temple Idol
treasure_idol_eye.lore: A green stone as big as a hen's egg, prised out of the face of a temple idol with its gold eyelid still on. Every story about a stone like this ends with someone being chased.

treasure_viking_arm_ring.name: Viking Silver Arm-Ring
treasure_viking_arm_ring.lore: A chieftain gave rings like this to his warriors, and a trader chopped bits off them to pay for things: silver went by its weight, not its look. One end has already been hacked off to buy something. Silver is heavy for what it is worth.

treasure_saxon_brooch.name: Saxon Garnet Brooch
treasure_saxon_brooch.lore: Gold set with hundreds of tiny garnet panels, each cut as thin as a fingernail and laid over gold foil so it throws the light back. Saxon kings went into the ground wearing work like this.

treasure_solidus_purse.name: Byzantine Solidus Purse
treasure_solidus_purse.lore: A pouch of gold solidi, the coin the emperor Constantine first struck. The emperors kept it the same weight of gold for seven hundred years, so merchants from Ireland to China trusted it. Honest old coin is worth more than its weight in gold.

treasure_celtic_torc.name: Celtic Gold Torc
treasure_celtic_torc.lore: A twisted neck-ring of gold, worn by Celtic chiefs and queens. A Roman historian wrote that Boudica rode into battle wearing a great twisted golden necklace. A pound of gold round the neck tells everyone who is in charge.

treasure_gulf_pearls.name: String of Gulf Pearls
treasure_gulf_pearls.lore: Natural pearls from the warm sea off Bahrain, where divers went down on a single breath with a stone tied to one foot, again and again from dawn to dusk. Every pearl on this string is a dive that found something.

treasure_silver_candelabra.name: Silver Candelabra
treasure_silver_candelabra.lore: Five branches of solid silver from some great house. Lovely, heavy, and worth less than its own weight in gold coin. A trader will give you something for it. Your back will give you nothing.

treasure_jade_bi.name: Liangzhu Jade Disc
treasure_jade_bi.lore: A bi, a flat disc of jade with a hole in the middle, laid on the dead in China five thousand years ago. Jade is too hard to cut with a knife: the Liangzhu people ground it with sand and water for months to make one.

treasure_arras_tapestry.name: Arras Tapestry
treasure_arras_tapestry.lore: Woven in Arras, a town so famous for its tapestries that English used its name for any wall hanging: Polonius hides behind an arras in Hamlet and does not come out alive. Twenty pounds of wool and silk. Priceless, and miserable to carry.

treasure_gold_idol.name: Gold Idol
treasure_gold_idol.lore: A squat idol of a god nobody prays to any more, cast in ten pounds of solid gold. Whoever made it was not trying to make it beautiful. Ten pounds is a lot to run with.

treasure_gold_rhyton.name: Persian Gold Rhyton
treasure_gold_rhyton.lore: The kings of ancient Persia drank from horns of solid gold like this one, each ending in a beast. This one ends in a winged lion, roaring. It is worth a city's taxes for a year.
